sections.h2: Where does a Licking County deed get recorded?
sections.html:
Deeds and mortgages for Licking County land go to the recorder's office at 20 S. Second Street in Newark, OH 43055. The recorder's page shows (740) 670-5300 for calls and (740) 670-5303 for fax, with the counter open from 8 AM to 4:30 PM on weekdays and recording running from 8:30 AM to 4:15 PM.

The office examines each document, assigns it a unique document number and a recording time, and uses that time to fix the order in which filings were made. Its records reach back to the early 1800s. Anyone can search the paper index and record books at the counter for no charge, and staff will help with the search.

Online viewing covers a window of more than two decades. A recorder's news item says documents recorded since September 22, 1997 can be viewed over the internet, including deeds, mortgages, releases, assignments and UCC statements. The same item looks back at 1999, when the office recorded 50,826 documents, among them 8,598 deeds and 13,895 mortgages, which it called its busiest year to that point.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Licking County?
sections.html:
The county posts its own recording sheet, and its formula reads: number of pages times $8, plus $23. A marginal reference costs $4. The fees page also announces a $5 preservation surcharge per document for standard document types as of January 1, 2025. Ask the recorder how the surcharge appears in your total before you write the check.

Licking County recording fees as printed on the county sheet
Document lengthFee
1 to 2 pages$39.00

Source: Licking County recording fees sheet. Other charges come from the Ohio Recorders' Association fee table the county also posts: photocopies and plat copies are $1.00 plus $1.00 per page, a certified copy is $1.00 plus $1.00 per page with a seal fee of 50 cents plus 50 cents, and a document that fails the state layout rules adds $10.00 plus $10.00.

sections.h2: Which documents does a Licking County recorder see around a house sale?
sections.html:
The state fee table groups a long list of instrument types under the basic page charge. These are the ones most tied to a sale, a payoff or an inheritance:

  • Warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, survivorship deeds and limited warranty deeds.
  • Executor's, administrator's, guardian's, trustee's and sheriff's deeds.
  • Certificates of transfer and transfer on death designation affidavits.
  • Mortgages, assignments, modifications, satisfactions and releases of lien.
  • Affidavits on facts relating to title, affidavits of surviving spouse and affidavits of successor trustee.
  • Memoranda of trust, powers of attorney, land contracts and easements.
  • Mechanic's liens, lis pendens notices and Medicaid estate recovery liens and their releases.

Military discharges and veteran grave summaries record without a fee under the same table. Federal tax liens carry their own listed charge of $5.00.

sections.h2: What happens at the Licking County auditor before the recorder?
sections.html:
No deed skips the auditor. Under section 319.202 the grantee, or an agent, declares the value conveyed, and the auditor stamps the deed with the fee. An exempt transfer needs only a stated reason.

Per the auditor's page, since May 1, 2026 a conveyance, exempt transfer, split or merge has to arrive by 4 p.m. to clear that day. That office is at 20 South Second Street, (740) 670-5040.

Sellers pay the state conveyance fee there. A county real property transfer tax would be collected at the same counter only if commissioners had enacted one under section 322.02, at no more than 30 cents per $100. Learn from the auditor whether it exists before choosing a closing date. When it does exist, payment precedes the trip to the recorder.

sections.h2: How can you search and watch Licking County records?
sections.html:
The recorder publishes a PaxWorld public access site at apps.lickingcounty.gov. It asks users to create an account with a username and password. Images that a user buys download to the user's computer, so the site tells visitors to allow downloads in the browser.

The same page promotes an AlertMe service that sends a notification when a document is recorded in your name. Older records can be searched at the recorder's counter, where the index is free.

Title companies, law firms and banks that file often can use eRecording. The county's page names four vendors:

  • CSC eRecording Solutions
  • ePN, the eRecording Partners Network
  • Indecomm Global Services
  • Simplifile

The recorder says electronic filing can cut turnaround from three to five working days to minutes or hours, and payment of recording fees is handled electronically.

sections.h2: What does the Census Bureau report about Licking County housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau QuickFacts table tallies 73,930 housing units for July 2025 and 68,620 households across the 2020 to 2024 survey years. Owned homes are valued around $275,200, and about three in four are lived in by the owner. Rent averages $1,078, and a homeowner with a loan pays about $1,693 monthly.

Population rose from 178,501 in April 2020 to an estimated 185,564 in July 2025. Newark is the county seat, and Wikipedia lists Heath, Johnstown, New Albany, Pataskala and Reynoldsburg as the other cities.

sections.h2: How does a payoff or an inheritance show up in the Licking County record?
sections.html:
A sale usually produces more than one recorded paper. The buyer's deed goes on record, and the seller's old mortgage is cleared by a satisfaction or release that the lender files. The state sheet lists satisfaction, release, partial release and cancellation as separate document types, and a marginal reference costs $4 when the recorder notes a link to an earlier filing.

Inherited property follows a different path. An executor's or administrator's deed, a certificate of transfer or a transfer on death designation affidavit can move title without a conventional sale, and each one is recorded like any other deed. If the owner received Medicaid benefits, the state table also lists a Medicaid estate recovery lien and its release as recordable instruments. Anyone who spots one of these in the chain should raise it with the title company before closing.

Veterans can record a military discharge with the recorder. The recorder's page names veterans discharges among the documents it accepts, and the state fee table shows no charge for a military discharge. Census data counts 11,370 veterans in Licking County for 2020 to 2024.

sections.h2: What should you know about Licking County's boundaries when searching old deeds?
sections.html:
The legislature carved Licking County out of Fairfield County in 1808, so the earliest history of a parcel may sit under the parent county's name. The recorder's holdings go back to the early 1800s, and the staff will help a searcher read the index. Seven counties touch Licking County, which means a parcel near a county line can carry a description that mentions Knox, Delaware, Franklin or another neighbor.

A rural parcel adds another wrinkle. The county ranks 11th among Ohio's 88 counties for farm products sold, and Wikipedia reports frequent developer offers for farmland near New Albany. A deed search for acreage should cover every transfer and any easements. The state table lists agricultural easements and conservation easements as their own document types.

faqs.q: When is the Licking County recorder open?
faqs.a: Staff are in from 8 AM until 4:30 PM on weekdays, and recording itself happens between 8:30 AM and 4:15 PM. Call (740) 670-5300 before a holiday.

faqs.q: What would a two-page Licking County deed cost to record?
faqs.a: The county sheet lists $39.00 for one to two pages, and its formula is pages times $8 plus $23. A third page brings the printed fee to $47.00.

faqs.q: Is searching Licking County records free?
faqs.a: Searching the index and record books at the recorder's counter is free. The online PaxWorld site requires an account, and purchased images download from the site.

faqs.q: Do I need the auditor before I record a Licking County deed?
faqs.a: Yes, the auditor endorses the deed and collects the conveyance fee first. For same-day processing the deed must reach the auditor by 4 p.m.

faqs.q: Can a title company e-record in Licking County?
faqs.a: Yes, the recorder accepts electronic filings through four listed eRecording vendors. Recorded documents come back electronically.
